pr.title: Make the analyzer work when SuppressSourceGeneration = true (REQ-2234)
pr.body:
Requirement: REQ-2234

Agent-written implementation of requirement REQ-2234 (upstream MessagePack-CSharp issue 2234), from the Junction 2026 challenge branch `ju26-issue-2234`.

Author: coding agent. Accountable owner: to be assigned by Countersign.
pr.author: ToukoUrsin

requirement.title: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true
requirement.body:
#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

criteria.text: In a project configured with SuppressSourceGeneration = true, the analyzer still runs and reports its diagnostics for code that violates its rules.
criteria.sourceQuote: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true.
criteria.note: Runs MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer on a [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] type with two [Key(0)] members and asserts the analyzer does not throw (no AD0001 or exception callback) and reports MsgPack005.

criteria.text: With SuppressSourceGeneration = true, no source is generated, while the analyzer diagnostics are still produced (the suppression affects generation only, not analysis).
criteria.note: For the same suppressed type with duplicate keys, runs MessagePackGenerator and asserts no generated source mentions the type and the generator does not fail (CS8785), and runs the analyzer and asserts MsgPack005 is reported without an analyzer exception.

criteria.text: For the same input code with SuppressSourceGeneration = true, the analyzer reports the same set of diagnostics as version 3.1.0 did.
criteria.sourceQuote: This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.
criteria.note: No executed evidence addresses this criterion. Contested by FN2 (verified in code): the tests that pass do not cover that case.

criteria.text: An automated test covers the analyzer with SuppressSourceGeneration = true and checks that at least one expected diagnostic is reported, so this regression would be caught.
criteria.sourceQuote: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true.
criteria.note: Runs the analyzer on a SuppressSourceGeneration = true type that mixes [Key(0)] and [Key("b")] and asserts it does not throw and reports at least one MsgPack005 diagnostic.

criteria.text: When SuppressSourceGeneration is false or not set, the analyzer still reports the same diagnostics and the generator still produces the same output as before the change.
criteria.note: Without SuppressSourceGeneration, asserts the analyzer reports exactly one MsgPack004 (for the member missing a key) with no exception, and the generator emits source for the valid NormalDto type without failing.

criteria.text: No existing analyzer or source-generator test regresses.
criteria.note: Supported by the regression run only; no test targets this criterion specifically.

story.headline: The type collector no longer throws on duplicate member keys, so the analyzer runs to completion and reports its key diagnostics (including for SuppressSourceGeneration types).
story.before: TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo added each keyed member with Dictionary.Add. If two members had the same int or string key, Add threw. The analyzer pass crashed and reported nothing, so users of SuppressSourceGeneration = true got no MsgPack diagnostics. The report says this started in 3.1.1.
story.after: Both member-collection loops check ContainsKey before adding. The first member with a given key is kept and later duplicates are dropped. A member whose key kind (int vs string) conflicts with earlier members gets the DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys diagnostic and is then skipped. The analyzer finishes and reports its diagnostics.

steps.text: In both member loops of TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo (fields and properties), intMembers/stringMembers.Add now runs only if the key is not already in the dictionary. The KeysMustBeUnique diagnostic is still reported for the duplicate, and the first member is kept.
After the DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys diagnostic, the loop now runs `continue`, so the conflicting member is not processed further with a null key.

New analyzer tests check that MsgPack003/004/005/015 are reported for suppressed types, that duplicate keys don't crash the analyzer for normal types, and that MsgPack011/016/017 are not reported for suppressed types.
Execution tests add a suppressed type. They check that GeneratedMessagePackResolver returns no formatter for it and that the type round-trips through the standard (dynamic) resolver.
The README gets a SuppressSourceGeneration section that lists which analyzer checks still apply (003, 004, 005, 012, 015) and which are skipped (011, 016, 017).

alsoTouches: The fix is in shared TypeCollector code, so it applies to every [MessagePackObject] type, not only types with SuppressSourceGeneration.

The source generator (MessagePackGenerator) uses the same collector. For a non-suppressed type with duplicate or mixed keys, it now produces a model where the extra members are dropped instead of throwing.
Members skipped because of mixed key kinds are no longer analyzed further, so diagnostics on their member types are no longer reported.
The README now documents which analyzer diagnostics apply to suppressed types.

diagrams.title: Duplicate/mixed-key handling in TypeCollector and who sees it
diagrams.caption: The change is in the shared TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo, so it affects both the analyzer and the source generator, not just suppressed types.

diagrams.title: Suppressed type with duplicate keys, analyzed in the IDE
diagrams.caption: Before, Dictionary.Add threw inside GetObjectInfo and the analyzer reported nothing. Now the duplicate is skipped and the diagnostics come through.

units.title: Keep first member on duplicate keys instead of throwing
units.summary: In both member-collection loops of TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo, a member is now added to intMembers/stringMembers only if its key is not already there. Before, Dictionary.Add threw on a duplicate key and crashed the analyzer, so no diagnostics were reported.

hunks.header: @@ -1617,6 +1617,20 @@ This code generation has a minor upfront performance cost.

lines.s: > Note: When using Unity, dynamic code generation only works when targeting .NET Framework 4.x + mono runtime.
For all other Unity targets, AOT is required.
A `[MessagePackObject]` type can opt out of source generation with `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]`.
No formatter is generated for that type. It is serialized at run time by the dynamic resolvers, which use reflection, so such a type is not AOT-safe.
The analyzer still validates these types, because they are serialized at run time and must still have a valid contract:
- Keys are unique and all of the same kind ([MsgPack005](doc/analyzers/MsgPack005.md)).
- Members have types that are themselves serializable ([MsgPack003](doc/analyzers/MsgPack003.md)).
- Types are accessible to the resolver ([MsgPack012](doc/analyzers/MsgPack012.md)).

The analyzer does not report the partial-class requirement ([MsgPack011](doc/analyzers/MsgPack011.md)) or the AOT-only checks ([MsgPack016](doc/analyzers/MsgPack016.md) and [MsgPack017](doc/analyzers/MsgPack017.md)) for these types, because they only apply when a formatter is generated.
You can customize the generated source through properties on the `GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute`.
continue; // The key kind does not match the other members; the diagnostic is reported, so skip this member.

findings.title: New `continue` on mixed keys skips recursive member-type analysis, including a case that never crashed
findings.body: The `continue` after `DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys` skips the rest of the loop body, including `this.CollectCore(item.Type, item)`. In the property loop, when the first key is a string and a later property has an int key, the old code did not throw: it reported MsgPack005, fell past both the `if (isIntKey)` and `else if (stringKey is not null)` branches, and still recursed into the member type. After this change the member's type is no longer analyzed, so its MsgPack003 and nested diagnostics disappear. In generator mode, generic, array and enum formatters reachable only through that member are no longer collected.

findings.title: Null-key field as first keyed member still throws in the collector
findings.body:
The PR aims to make invalid keys report without an analyzer failure, but one sibling crash path remains. In the field loop, when the first keyed member is a field with `[Key(null)]`, `searchFirst` sets `isIntKey = false`, the mix check is skipped, and the unconditional `else` branch calls `stringMembers.ContainsKey(stringKey!)` with null. That throws ArgumentNullException (AD0001 in the analyzer, a generator failure in generator mode). The property loop avoids this with `else if (stringKey is not null)`; the field loop has no such guard. The existing NullStringKey test covers only a property.

Note: the skeptic judged this defect to pre-date this PR.

findings.title: Generator now emits a formatter that silently omits duplicate/mixed-key members
findings.body: TypeCollector is shared with the source generator, which calls it with `reportAnalyzerDiagnostic: null`. Before, a duplicate key made `Dictionary.Add` throw inside the generator, so no output was produced. Now the first member wins, the later one is dropped, and a formatter is generated for the reduced contract. The only remaining signal is the analyzer's MsgPack005. If that is suppressed or downgraded, the generated formatter loses the member's data without any error. No test covers generator output for these inputs.
findings.scenario: `[MessagePackObject] class Foo { [Key(0)] public string A {get;set;} [Key(0)] public string B {get;set;} }` with MsgPack005 set to none/warning. The build succeeds and the generated formatter serializes only A; B is silently lost on round-trip.
